title: Thick fossil-rich formations accumulate during subsidence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Thick fossil-rich formations accumulate during subsidence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Fossiliferous formations thick and extensive enough to survive later erosion are formed in shallow seas during periods of slow subsidence in which the supply of sediment roughly keeps pace with sinking.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I am convinced that all our ancient formations, which are rich in fossils, have thus been formed during subsidence.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the intermittence of geological formations”. Scope: marine sedimentary formations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-06: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.83

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The predicted geological associations are measurable at broad scale with public data. Standard basin and comparative analyses can distinguish subsidence from alternative settings.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate formation thickness, fossil richness, depositional depth, tectonic subsidence histories, and sediment accumulation rates. Concentration of thick fossil-rich units in slowly subsiding shallow basins with accommodation matched by sediment supports the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Subsidence histories require regional models.

Present thickness reflects compaction and later erosion.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.86
data adequacy: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.76
data existence: 0.94
analysis feasibility: 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Thickness, environment, and fossil counts are downloadable and can be joined, so the association is testable in studied basins within weeks to a few months. Circularity between thickness and inferred subsidence is the main limit on discriminating power. The result would cover a large marine sample and still fall short of every ancient fossiliferous formation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Relate formation thickness and fossil richness in shallow-marine units to independent evidence of subsidence, such as tectonic setting and backstripping, not to thickness alone. A positive association during slow subsidence with sediment keeping pace would support the claim; thick fossil-rich sections formed mainly during uplift or non-depositional deepening would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Thickness is often used to infer subsidence, which makes the association partly circular.

The wording 'all our ancient formations' is stronger than any basin sample.

Independent tectonic evidence is uneven outside well-studied basins.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.72
data existence: 0.74
discriminating power: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.66
